text:
mika: Customer (AcmeGames) reports intermittent JSON parse failures from our streaming JSON mode. Parser error: \"Unexpected end of JSON input\". Happens roughly every 50-120s. They also see a 401 in our access logs right before the truncation. req_id=acme-req-72f. Can someone triage? cc @ryan @alex

ryan: Do we have the exact request they used? SSE vs chunked? Any reverse proxy in front of their client?

mika: They said chunked transfer to /v1/stream/chat with Accept: text/event-stream and Authorization: Bearer <token>. Client is a mobile app behind a carrier NAT + their nginx reverse proxy. Here's the curl they sent (redacted token):

```bash
curl -N -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \\n  'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream/chat?mode=json_structured&prompt=hello'
```

alex: 401 midstream feels like token refresh race or proxy closing the TCP connection. We don't accept new Authorization headers mid-connection. If the client tries to rotate tokens without reconnecting, server will treat new frames as unauthorized. Also proxies can send FIN leading to truncated last chunk.

mika: Attaching customer-provided server-side snippets (sanitized):

```
[2026-02-12T12:03:34Z] req_id=acme-req-72f method=POST path=/v1/stream/chat status=200 stream_open
[2026-02-12T12:04:21Z] req_id=acme-req-72f auth=expired status=401 token_rotate_detected
[2026-02-12T12:04:21Z] req_id=acme-req-72f stream_end=client_closed bytes_sent=23456
```

support-bot: Created ticket CS-1234 for this thread.

ryan: I pulled our traces for req_id=acme-req-72f — initial handshake ok, then an auth failure at ~47s which correlates with the stream being cut. Looking at TCP flags indicates a FIN from the client/proxy side not a server RST. Their LB has a 45s idle timeout.

alex: Two action paths: 1) immediate customer workarounds (heartbeats / NDJSON / tolerant parser). 2) infra mitigation (emit periodic keepalive, make structured streaming tolerant of partial last object). For immediate: suggest they switch to ndjson (newline-delimited JSON objects) or add a small comment heartbeat for SSE (e.g., `:hb\n\n`) every 20s so carrier NAT/LB sees activity.

mika: Customer wants repro steps to validate on their side. Proposed reproducer (they can run locally to simulate a short NAT timeout):

```bash
# open streaming connection then kill after 48s to simulate carrier NAT/proxy close
TOKEN=REDACTED
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \\n  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream/chat?mode=json_structured&prompt=test" &
PID=$!
sleep 48
kill -9 $PID
```

Then attempt to parse the partial output with a tolerant reader; you'll see last object may be cut mid-field.

ryan: Also ask them: are they rotating short-lived tokens (STS) on the mobile client? If so, they must re-open the stream after a token rotation. We should note this in docs: Authorization header cannot be updated in-flight.

alex: For engineering follow-up I'll: 1) spin up a controlled internal endpoint that emits N structured JSON objects with configurable delays so we can reproduce with different proxy timeout values; 2) add logging to surface connection close reason (FIN vs RST) and publish to the ticket.

mika: Customer reported their nginx has proxy_read_timeout=60s but their carrier resets idle earlier (~45s). They also said their client sometimes tries to refresh token in the background which coincides with the midstream 401.

ryan: Immediate customer recommendations to minimize outages:
- Use ndjson / newline-delimited JSON for streaming consumers that must survive mid-connection interruption.
- Add a client-side tolerant JSON stream parser (incremental parse) rather than expecting one single JSON object/array.
- Implement heartbeat comments for SSE or periodic 1-byte flushes from our side.
- If rotating tokens, re-open the stream after obtaining a new token; don't attempt to swap header midstream.

mika: I'm marking CS-1234 P1 since they are in production and parsing failures are crashing their ingestion pipeline. Alex/Ryan — can you post a small repro trace link and ETA?

alex: Creating the internal repro endpoint now and will post trace link when ready (will try to reproduce with 30s/45s/90s timeouts). Tentative ETA 4h.

ryan: Pasted trace: https://internal.redwood/traces/abc123 (internal). Also added a debug flag on nginx-ingress to correlate request IDs.

mika: Thanks team. I'll relay ndjson and heartbeat workarounds to the customer and attach the repro script + our engineering notes. :pray:
